info.title: fleetd API
info.description: Versioned control-plane contract for cooperating software agents.

get.description: Operator-only. Lists profile references, standing instructions, desired state, and restart revisions. Executables, arguments, tool grants, environment, and harness credentials are private to the machine-local profile catalog and never cross this boundary.

Operator-only. Projects each stable agent identity as unmanaged, idle, working, interrupted, recovery-required, or offline from exact durable generation, session, invocation, progress, and delivery evidence. Lease and fence credentials are never returned.

get.summary: Read what the fleet is doing now
get.description: Operator-only. One durable read reporting the current plugin generation per agent, the current generation of each session binding, the invocations still owed an outcome, and a delivery census including leases whose window has closed.

parameters.name: agent
parameters.description: Limit the report to one agent ID.

parameters.name: delivery_limit
parameters.description: Bound how many delivery rows the census reads.

get.description: Operator-only. Reports event counts, chain digests, terminal state, and usage without duplicating raw transcripts. Ordered by `updated_at_ms`, the clock every folded event advances and which freezes once an invocation is terminal. A collector walks `order=oldest` and resumes from the last row's `updated_at_ms` and `invocation_id`; `settled=true` reports only terminal rows, whose evidence never changes again.

parameters.name: agent
parameters.description: Limit results to one agent ID.

parameters.name: after_ms
parameters.description: Exclusive change-clock cursor. Must be supplied with `after_id`.

parameters.name: after_id
parameters.description: Exclusive row-ID tiebreak. Must be supplied with `after_ms`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Requested page size. Values above 500 are clamped to 500.

parameters.name: settled
parameters.description: Report only rows whose evidence can never change again.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Direction the change clock is walked. Walk `oldest` to archive.

200.description: One page of bounded invocation observations

A collector walks `order=oldest` and resumes from the last row's `last_heartbeat_at_ms` and `id`.

AckDelivery.description: Input for acknowledging a successfully processed delivery.

AddMember.description: Input for adding one agent to a channel.

AdvanceConversationRead.description: Advances the authenticated participant's durable read cursor.

through_seq.description: Highest channel message sequence the participant has observed.

Agent.description: An addressable participant in the fleet.

AgentSeat.description:
Credential-free operational projection of one stable agent identity.

Joins the current worker generation, the native-session lane, the managed
invocation, and the delivery it came from, so an operator can see a seat that
needs recovery without correlating four endpoints by hand.

AgentSeatConfiguration.description:
Operator-selected execution for one stable agent identity.

`profile_id` is only a reference. Executable paths, arguments, environment,
tool grants, and harness credentials stay in a private catalog on the host.

AgentSeatDesiredState.description: Whether the machine hosting an approved runtime should keep an agent active.

AgentSeatReason.description: The exact durable evidence responsible for a projected seat state.

AgentSeatState.description:
Current operator-facing state of one durable agent seat.

Derived from evidence rather than stored, so unlike the enums the substrate
persists this needs no string codec: it is only ever serialised outward.

ArmInvocation.description: Input for the write-ahead fence immediately before effectful dispatch.

Binding.description: Fleet-owned identity for one logical session lane.

BlockDelivery.description: Input for parking an ambiguously executed delivery under its active lease.

BlockResolution.description: Operator decision for a blocked delivery.

BlockedDelivery.description: One unresolved blocked delivery and its immutable source message.

BrowserStreamCursor.description: A valid exclusive cursor in Fleetd's signed global message sequence.

BrowserStreamGrant.description: One validated raw stream-grant token. Debug output is always redacted.

BrowserStreamGrantIssueRequest.description: Strict authenticated request to mint one browser stream grant.

BrowserStreamGrantIssueResponse.description: One-time response to successful browser stream grant issuance.

BrowserStreamPath.description: Exact path returned by successful grant issuance.

BrowserStreamProtocol.description:
Exact browser stream protocol negotiated during upgrade and bound into a
grant. Representing the constant as a closed enum makes alternate values
fail during JSON decoding and constrains its generated schema.

BrowserStreamRedemptionRequest.description:
The only application message accepted before browser stream authority is
established. It carries no caller-selected channel, cursor, or principal.

BrowserStreamServerFrame.description:
Tagged server-to-browser application frames. The immutable message
envelope is nested without translation or field selection.

Channel.description: A durable conversation shared by a bounded set of agents.

ChannelMember.description: Bounded public membership projection without opaque agent metadata.

ClaimBatch.description: A set of deliveries owned by one expiring lease token.

ClaimDeliveries.description: Input for atomically leasing work from an agent inbox.

CompleteInvocation.description: Input for atomically publishing one result and acknowledging its invocation.

ConfigureAgentSeat.description: Bounded operator request to configure one agent's approved local runtime.

ConversationAttention.description:
Exact unread state for one authenticated participant in one conversation.

The projection is derived only from the participant's durable membership
cursor and immutable message envelopes. The participant's own messages are
not unread. `addressed_unread_count` counts messages from another
participant whose exact `recipient_id` is the reader; it does not infer
urgency from message content.

ConversationKind.description: The durable conversation lifecycle selected by fleetd.

ConversationSummary.description: One conversation with bounded participant and recency metadata for clients.

CreateChannel.description: Input for creating a shared channel and its initial membership.

CreateChannelMember.description: Exact initial membership used by the durable store.

Delivery.description: One leased inbox entry and the immutable message it carries.

DeliveryCensus.description:
A census of durable delivery rows by state, plus the leases among them
whose window has already closed.

`inspected` is how many rows the census actually read, which a bounded
read model may cap below the true total.

DeliveryRecord.description: Read-only operator projection of one durable delivery.

DeliveryState.description: Durable inbox state exposed to the operator without lease credentials.

ErrorResponse.description: Stable JSON envelope returned for fleetd domain errors.

EvidenceOrder.description:
Which way a cursor-addressed evidence listing walks the change clock.

An operator reads `Newest` first. A collector archiving every row walks
`Oldest` from its last position, so rows appended or changed while it was
away arrive ahead of it rather than behind it.

ExecutionCertainty.description: What fleetd can prove about an invocation's external execution.

FleetHealth.description:
What a fleet is doing right now, as one durable read.

"Current" means the newest generation for each agent and the newest
generation of each session binding; older rows for the same key are
history, not health. Invocations are the ones still owed an outcome.

Invocation.description: One durable managed attempt reserved together with its inbox lease.

InvocationBatch.description: A batch of delivery attempts atomically leased and durably reserved.

InvocationCompletion.description: Durable result of completing one managed invocation.

InvocationEventCounts.description: Fixed-size event counters retained for one managed invocation.

prompt.description:
The prompt Fleetd sent, echoed back by the harness. It is also where the
envelope adapter's invocation id appears in a replayed transcript.

InvocationObservation.description:
Bounded operational evidence for one managed invocation and its exact
source/result message relationship.

Raw update streams are represented by exact byte counts and a chain digest;
the bounded result message remains the transcript authority.

InvocationState.description: Durable lifecycle state for one managed delivery attempt.

InvocationTrace.description:
Exact operator trace joining one invocation to its bounded harness,
plugin-generation, native-session, and result evidence.

A reserved invocation carries none of it yet. Once an observation exists,
the session and plugin generation it names must still be readable, so a
present observation with an absent session is an integrity error rather
than an empty field.

IssuedCredential.description:
A newly issued credential. Its token is returned once and never persisted
in plaintext by fleetd.

MembershipDeliveryMode.description: Whether one channel membership receives leased inbox work.

Message.description: An immutable message envelope in the global event sequence.

MessagePage.description: A cursor-addressed page from a channel's message history.

ObservedPluginInterface.description: One exact operational interface observed on a plugin generation.

OpenDirectConversation.description: Input for idempotently opening a one-to-one direct conversation.

members.description:
Exactly two distinct participants. Their delivery modes become
immutable with the direct conversation.

PluginGeneration.description: Durable operator read model for one ready plugin generation.

PluginGenerationDisposition.description: Why a worker stopped routing work through one plugin generation.

PluginGenerationHealth.description: Operator-facing liveness derived from persisted state and heartbeat age.

PluginGenerationState.description: Persisted lifecycle state of one ready plugin generation.

PluginShutdownOutcome.description: What Fleetd observed while terminating a plugin process group.

RegisterTrigger.description:
What an operator declares when registering a trigger.

`sender_id` names an existing agent rather than introducing a principal of
its own. A trigger's messages are attributable to a durable identity that
already exists, and the kernel's six concepts are unchanged; what is new is
the credential, which may do this and nothing else.

accepted_kinds.description:
The exact kinds this trigger may create. Non-empty, deduplicated, and
part of the trigger's identity: changing it changes what the trigger is.

RegisteredAgent.description: An agent registration and its one-time credential response.

RegisteredTrigger.description:
A trigger registration and its one-time credential response.

Registering and being able to fire are one act. A trigger holding no
credential is inert, and a credential naming a trigger that does not exist is
authority over nothing, so neither is a state fleetd will hand back.

RenameChannel.description: Input for renaming a shared channel.

ResolveDeliveryBlock.description: Input for resolving one exact blocked-delivery record.

RetireTrigger.description:
Why an operator is ending a trigger's standing grant.

Required rather than optional. A retired trigger with no reason recorded
leaves the next operator guessing whether it was decommissioned or switched
off in an incident, which is exactly the question the record exists to
answer.

RetryDelivery.description: Input for releasing a failed delivery for a later attempt.

SendMessage.description:
Authenticated input for sending a message. The server supplies `sender_id`
from the bound agent credential.

SessionBinding.description: One durable native-session generation and its current owner fence.

SessionBindingState.description: Durable lifecycle state for one native harness session generation.

Trigger.description:
One registered trigger, as an operator reads it.

The firing history is the reason to register a trigger at all. A crontab
entry that stopped firing on Tuesday leaves no trace, and an idle fleet looks
exactly like a healthy quiet one; `last_fired_at_ms` is what turns that
absence into a fact.

last_occurrence_id.description: The last occurrence Fleetd accepted from this trigger, and when.

TriggerFired.description:
What Fleetd answers when a trigger fires.

`created` distinguishes a firing that produced work from one Fleetd
recognised as a repeat. An unattended scheduler cannot tell the difference on
its own, and the difference is the whole reason idempotency lives here.

TriggerOccurrence.description:
What a trigger supplies when it fires.

Deliberately small. Sender, channel, correlation, causation, and the durable
idempotency key are all derived from the registration, so this carries only
what the trigger actually knows: which firing this is, who should act, and
what to say.

occurrence_id.description:
The trigger's own name for this firing. Fleetd derives the durable
idempotency key from the trigger and this together, so a repeat is
absorbed exactly and two triggers cannot collide on one key.

TriggerState.description: Whether a trigger may still create work.
